context:
Data: Eurostat HICP, euro area* = the 21 current members at every date, chain-linked bottom-up from six components. Last published month: Sep 2026. The forecast covers the next three months.
Selected component models (pre-committed rule: keep the simpler model unless a richer one is significantly better, Diebold-Mariano test, chosen on 2010-2019 origins): fuels: Weekly Oil Bulletin pump prices; electricity and gas: seasonal mean of monthly changes; processed food: AR(p) chosen by AIC; unprocessed food: seasonal mean of monthly changes; non-energy industrial goods: AR(p), rolling 120-month window; services: seasonal mean, rolling 120-month window.
Base effect = the part of the change in y/y that comes from the monthly change a year earlier dropping out; it is known in advance. Momentum = the part from new monthly price changes.
The bands are empirical quantiles of the model's own past out-of-sample errors, not model-implied.
The shock simulator moves price levels per country and component; second-round effects are an estimated distributed lag. Actuals are final Eurostat releases; flash estimates are used only in the real-time check.
Not modelled: country forecasts (only the euro area* headline is forecast and backtested), core inflation as a target, ECB policy decisions, anything after the three-month horizon.
Italy: its published total differs from the weighted sum of its components by up to about a tenth of a point; the cause is not identified.
